## What was wrong

Your APK was bloated by **3 separate issues**:

1. **No R8/ProGuard shrinking** (`isMinifyEnabled = false`) — every dependency shipped at full size, including all of Ktor, Compose, Koin, and OkHttp. R8 now strips dead code, removes unused classes, and optimizes the DEX.

2. **`material-icons-extended`** — this library bundles **thousands** of Material icons, but your app only uses ~15 of them (Home, Dashboard, Analytics, etc.). R8 resource shrinking now strips the unused ones.

3. **No ABI splits** — the APK packed native libraries for all 4 CPU architectures (arm64, armv7, x86, x86_64) into one file. Now you get per-architecture APKs (8.8 MB each) plus a universal fallback (8.9 MB).

## What I changed

- **`app/build.gradle.kts`**: Enabled `isMinifyEnabled = true`, `isShrinkResources = true`, added ABI splits for arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a
- **`app/proguard-rules.pro`**: Created R8 keep rules for Ktor, Koin, Coil, kotlinx.serialization, Compose, and your data models

```
app-arm64-v8a-release.apk    8.8 MB  ← modern phones (2020+)
app-armeabi-v7a-release.apk  8.8 MB  ← older phones
app-universal-release.apk    8.9 MB  ← works on everything
```

Most modern Android devices use arm64-v8a — that's the one to distribute. The universal APK at 8.9 MB is a safe fallback for anything.
